s: Express middleware chain in server.js: morgan logging, JSON parser, route mounting, static file serving, and global error handler.
Controllers use express-async-handler wrapping, throwing errors that propagate to global error middleware without explicit try/catch.
Multer configured in uploadRoutes.js with disk storage to uploads/, validating .jpg/.jpeg/.png extensions and MIME types.
MongoDB collections: users (bcrypt password, isAdmin), products (with embedded Review sub-schema and computed rating).
Order collection with embedded order items, shipping address, payment/delivery timestamps, and cross-collection references to User and Product.
PayPal sandbox integration using react-paypal-button-v2 with dynamic SDK loading and client ID fetched from server config endpoint.
Deployment setup: Docker Compose for MongoDB, npm scripts for dev workflow, Heroku Procfile with heroku-postbuild for production.
Cross-cutting concerns: protect/admin JWT middleware, global error handler, CORS configuration, and server-side input validation.
Architecture strengths: uniform async pattern across controllers, granular Redux slices, and localStorage persistence for cart/auth.
Known technical debt: JWT in localStorage (XSS risk), no rate limiting, missing server-side order validation, no health check endpoint.
Practical guidance for production-grade MERN e-commerce, using proshop_mern as a deliberately legacy reference for 2026 best practices.
Modern MERN patterns: TypeScript end-to-end, Vite replacing CRA, Fastify as Express alternative, Node.js 22 LTS, Atlas connection pooling.
Production monitoring: Winston for structured JSON logs, Sentry for error tracking, health check endpoints for load balancers.
Mongoose schema best practices: embed one-to-few, reference one-to-many, compound indexes for real queries, lean() for read-only endpoints.
Mongoose patterns: virtuals for computed values, hooks for pre/post operations, and soft deletes over hard deletes for data recovery.
Cursor-based pagination with _id filtering is O(log n) vs offset-based O(n), critical for large product catalogs.
Redux state management: RTK Query vs TanStack Query selection criteria, cache invalidation via tags, optimistic cart updates.
Best practice: separate server state (products, orders) from client state (cart, auth) using RTK Query for server data caching.
PayPal 2026 patterns: webhook-driven payment confirmation, idempotency keys via PayPal-Request-Id, and webhook signature verification.
PayPal safety: idempotent webhook handlers for up to 25 retries, sandbox/live environment separation, double-charge prevention at order level.
JWT security: never store in localStorage, use short-lived access tokens with refresh token rotation via HttpOnly cookies.
Security layers: CSP headers for XSS defense, rate limiting on auth endpoints, and JWT algorithm lockdown to prevent alg:none attacks.
E-commerce performance targets: LCP under 2.5s, FID under 100ms, CLS under 0.1, with performance budgets and image optimization pipeline.
Server-side performance: TTFB under 200ms via CDN edge caching, query optimization, and frontend list virtualization for large catalogs.
Feature flag strategies: decouple deployment from release, OpenFeature vendor-neutral standard, progressive canary rollouts.
Feature flags enable backend A/B testing for search ranking, recommendations, pricing, and checkout flow optimization.
RBAC pattern: assign permissions to roles not users, store permissions in database, scale access control without code changes.
Admin dashboard patterns: immutable audit log for all admin actions, bulk operation safety with dry-run, and authorization failure logging.
Server-side permission checks are mandatory — client-side role hiding is UX only, the API must enforce authorization on every request.
Concrete migration patterns for proshop_mern: move JWT to HttpOnly cookies, add Mongoose indexes, add webhook verification, improve error handling.
Actionable improvements: add PayPal idempotency header, register webhook endpoint, implement React.lazy code splitting, optimize images.
Reliability patterns: health check endpoint, graceful SIGTERM shutdown, MongoDB connection pooling, circuit breaker for external APIs.

Early release notes: v0.1 scaffold, v0.3 cart with localStorage, v0.5 JWT auth, v0.6 server-side order total fix, v0.8 PayPal SDK.
Major releases: v1.0 review system + Redux Toolkit migration, v1.2 pagination + search, v1.5 image upload, v1.7 route security patch.

Key decision: chose MongoDB over PostgreSQL for variable product attributes, with acknowledgment that PostgreSQL would have been equally valid.
Decision to stay on Bootstrap 4 (deferred Tailwind migration) and use JWT over session cookies for stateless authentication.

Server-side order total recalculation should have been in v0.1; TLS termination, better error handling, and CI/CD are areas for improvement.
Authoritative reference for the features.json format and MCP server contract with three tools for managing feature flag lifecycle.
Feature flags in this ProShop project: 25 flags managing product search, cart, checkout, payments, admin, and UX features.
features.json schema: each feature has required fields (name, status, traffic_percentage, last_modified) and optional fields (dependencies, segments).
Status semantics: Disabled (0%, off), Testing (1-99%, gradual), Enabled (100%, fully on) with automatic traffic percentage rules.
MCP tool 1: get_feature_info reads features.json on every call, returns full flag state including dependency status.
MCP tool 2: set_feature_state changes flag status with automatic traffic adjustment and dependency validation warnings.
MCP tool 3: adjust_traffic_rollout changes traffic percentage on Testing flags only, validates 0-100 range.
Complete catalog of 25 feature flags organized by domain: search, cart, checkout, payments, admin, performance, and UX.
search_v2 flag: new search algorithm using Elasticsearch or Atlas Search to replace MongoDB regex, currently in Testing at 15%.
cart_redesign flag: redesigned cart UI with responsive layout and inline quantity editing, Testing at 10% traffic.
express_checkout flag: one-click checkout for returning users with saved shipping, currently Disabled pending implementation.
paypal_express_buttons flag: PayPal Smart Payment Buttons on cart and product screens, fully Enabled at 100%.
product_recommendations flag: ML-powered 'Customers also bought' section on product pages, Testing at 30%.
admin_dashboard_v2 flag: unified admin dashboard with charts and analytics replacing table-heavy screens, currently Disabled.
reviews_moderation flag: admin review moderation queue where new reviews require approval before publishing, currently Disabled.
image_lazy_loading flag: native loading='lazy' attribute on product images, fully Enabled at 100% for performance.
dark_mode flag: sun/moon toggle in Header switching between light and dark CSS custom property themes, Testing at 20%.
Rollout strategies: canary deployment (5%→25%→100%) and A/B testing (50/50 split) for measuring feature impact with statistical rigor.
Kill switch pattern: keeping deployed features under a flag for instant disabling without code deployment, e.g., disabling PayPal in emergencies.
Flag best practices: mandatory lifecycle with cleanup deadlines, avoid dependency chains, remove flags after feature is permanent.
Development flag testing: environment variable overrides for local testing, security considerations for admin-only flags.
Admin navigation: conditional admin menu in Header.js based on isAdmin flag, protected by protect + admin middleware chain on backend.
Admin product list: paginated table with create/edit/delete actions, product create generates sample template for editing.
Admin product create: generates sample product with placeholder values, immediately opens edit form for filling real data.
Admin product edit: form with name, price, image URL or file upload, brand, category, countInStock, description fields.
Product edit edge cases: no min/max validation on price/stock, upload path overwrites image URL field on submit.
Admin product delete: permanent removal with browser confirmation dialog, calls DELETE /api/products/:id endpoint.
Admin user list: table with ID, name, email (mailto link), admin status, and edit/delete action buttons.
Admin user edit: form to modify name, email, and isAdmin checkbox with success redirect to user list.
Admin user delete: removes user account while preserving their orders in database (no cascade delete).
Admin order list: table showing all orders with user, date, total, paid/delivered status, and details navigation.
Admin mark delivered: sets isDelivered=true and deliveredAt timestamp on paid orders via PUT /api/orders/:id/deliver.
Image upload for products: client-side form uploads via POST /api/uploads, multer saves to uploads/, returns file path.
Upload edge cases: files over 2MB rejected by multer, unsupported types (GIF, WebP) rejected, upload errors shown in console only.
User login: email/password authentication on LoginScreen, dispatches login action, stores JWT token in Redux state + localStorage.
Login edge cases: wrong email/password returns 401, redirect query parameter preserved through login flow, form prevents empty submission.
